base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan an Easter brunch for their extended family by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and preferences. When asked to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates to restrictions throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm hosting Easter brunch this Sunday for the family. Can you help me figure out the menu?

flow_info.value: Coming so far: me, my sister Rachel, my brother-in-law Tom, and my mom
Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Tom ate shrimp at a wedding two years ago and his throat swelled shut, had to use an EpiPen
Mom's been managing type 2 diabetes for a while now
My cousin Amy just confirmed she's coming too, with her husband Derek
Derek is a pretty adventurous eater, no restrictions at all
I'm thinking around 200 dollars total for everything, feeding about 6-7 people
Tom just told Rachel he got called into work Sunday morning, so he won't make it. But he asked if I could save him a plate

Mom called me — her doctor switched her to a new medication that controls her blood sugar really well now, she said she can have normal portions of everything including dessert, no need to worry about sugar for her anymore
Oh, Rachel is bringing her daughter Lily too, she's 4. Lily broke out in hives last month after eating scrambled eggs at daycare

I'm looking at making: eggs Benedict with hollandaise, a smoked salmon quiche with a regular pie crust, shrimp and grits, a fruit salad with honey-lime dressing, and hot cross buns from the bakery that are labeled gluten-free. How does that look?

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or cross-contaminated products
constraints.surface_form: Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye

constraints.value: Cannot eat shellfish — shrimp, crab, lobster, etc.
constraints.surface_form: Tom ate shrimp at a wedding two years ago and his throat swelled shut, had to use an EpiPen

constraints.value: Cannot eat eggs or egg-containing products
constraints.surface_form: Lily broke out in hives last month after eating scrambled eggs at daycare
inference_chain: Hives after eating scrambled eggs → allergic reaction to eggs
Egg allergy → must avoid eggs and egg-containing products

hidden_state.value: You are hosting Easter brunch for extended family. You will share guest details, dietary info, and updates across several turns. Some guests will join, one will drop out but want a saved plate, and one medical constraint will be removed. At the end you will present a specific menu and ask how it looks. You never hint at what the problems might be — you genuinely think the menu sounds good.

You are a calm, warm family organizer. You always refer to family members by name in third person (e.g. 'Rachel told me...', 'Tom said...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal family coordination for a holiday gathering.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family updates

aims.description: Hey, I'm hosting Easter brunch this Sunday for the family. Can you help me figure out the menu?

So it's me, my sister Rachel, my brother-in-law Tom, and my mom coming so far. Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year. Tom ate shrimp at a wedding two years ago and his throat swelled shut — had to use an EpiPen. And my mom's been managing type 2 diabetes for a while now.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges all attendees and their dietary constraints
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver 4 entities with 3 constraints in one burst

aims.description: My cousin Amy just confirmed she's coming too, with her husband Derek. Derek is a pretty adventurous eater, no restrictions at all. I'm thinking around 200 dollars total for everything, feeding about 6-7 people.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Amy and Derek joining, notes budget

aims.description: Should I do a sit-down thing or more of a buffet spread? There's going to be kids running around so I'm leaning buffet.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about format without losing track of dietary constraints

drift_config.drift_topic: sit-down vs buffet style for Easter brunch

aims.description: Tom just told Rachel he got called into work Sunday morning, so he won't make it. But he asked if I could save him a plate.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Tom exits the brunch but needs a saved plate — his shellfish allergy applies to the saved plate
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT with scope change — Tom's shellfish allergy now applies to saved plate only

aims.description: Mom called me — her doctor switched her to a new medication that controls her blood sugar really well now. She said she can have normal portions of everything including dessert, no need to worry about sugar for her anymore.
aims.success_criteria: Agent removes mom's diabetes dietary restriction
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL — mom's diabetes restriction lifted

aims.description: Oh, Rachel is bringing her daughter Lily too, she's 4. Lily broke out in hives last month after eating scrambled eggs at daycare.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Lily as new attendee with egg allergy
aims.conversation_goal: Late-joining high-constraint entity — Lily with egg allergy

aims.description: What time do you think works best? I was thinking 11am so people aren't rushing to get here too early.

drift_config.drift_topic: what time to start Easter brunch

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn to create distance before probe

aims.description: Do you think I need to set up a separate kids' table or just let them sit with us?

drift_config.drift_topic: kids table vs family table for brunch

aims.conversation_goal: Additional noise turn to maximize distance before probe

aims.description: I'm looking at making: eggs Benedict with hollandaise, a smoked salmon quiche with a regular pie crust, shrimp and grits, a fruit salad with honey-lime dressing, and hot cross buns from the bakery that are labeled gluten-free. How does that look?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: eggs Benedict problematic for Lily (contains eggs in hollandaise AND poached egg); smoked salmon quiche problematic for Rachel (regular pie crust contains gluten) AND for Lily (quiche contains eggs); shrimp and grits fine for the table but cannot be saved for Tom's plate (shellfish allergy); fruit salad fine for everyone; hot cross buns labeled gluten-free are fine for Rachel
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Eggs Benedict: problematic for Lily — hollandaise sauce contains egg yolks and the dish has a poached egg (egg allergy). Smoked salmon quiche with regular pie crust: problematic for Rachel — regular pie crust is made with wheat flour (celiac/gluten), AND problematic for Lily — quiche contains eggs. Shrimp and grits: fine for the table (Tom is not attending the brunch), but must NOT be included in Tom's saved plate (shellfish allergy — anaphylactic). Fruit salad with honey-lime dressing: fine for everyone. Hot cross buns labeled gluten-free: fine for Rachel and everyone else — the gluten-free label means they are safe for celiac.
required_elements: Eggs Benedict is problematic for Lily because it contains eggs (hollandaise has egg yolks, dish includes poached egg) and Lily has an egg allergy
Smoked salmon quiche is problematic for Rachel because the regular pie crust contains wheat flour (gluten) and Rachel has celiac disease
Smoked salmon quiche is also problematic for Lily because quiche contains eggs and Lily has an egg allergy
Shrimp and grits is fine for the table but must NOT be saved for Tom's plate because Tom has a shellfish allergy (anaphylactic reaction to shrimp)
Fruit salad with honey-lime dressing is fine for everyone currently attending
Hot cross buns labeled gluten-free are acceptable for Rachel — agent confirms they are safe
forbidden_elements: Flagging sugar content as a problem for mom (her diabetes restriction has been removed by her doctor)
Saying Tom's shellfish allergy means shrimp and grits cannot be served at the brunch table (Tom is not attending, only needs a saved plate)
Flagging smoked salmon as a shellfish issue (salmon is fish, not shellfish — Tom's allergy is specifically shellfish)
Saying Lily has a general food allergy beyond eggs (she specifically reacted to eggs only)
Flagging hot cross buns as problematic for Rachel when they are labeled gluten-free
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 10 conversational turns. Key tracking challenges: (1) Rachel has celiac disease → must infer no gluten → regular pie crust contains wheat flour (hidden ingredient trap: quiche looks like a safe salmon dish but the CRUST is the problem). (2) Tom EXITS the brunch but needs a saved plate — his shellfish allergy applies only to what goes on his plate, not to what's served at the table. (3) Mom's diabetes restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (new medication). (4) Lily JOINS late (Turn 6) with an egg allergy — the primary failure mode: models forget late-joining entities. Eggs Benedict contains eggs in BOTH the hollandaise sauce and the poached egg itself. The quiche also contains eggs. (5) The over-generalization trap: Tom's allergy is to shellfish (shrimp), NOT all seafood — smoked salmon is fine. (6) The scope distinction: shrimp and grits is fine for the buffet table but cannot go on Tom's saved plate.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
